booklet.title: GenroPy Runner: a desktop window with card signing
booklet.author: Giovanni Porcari

purpose.p: How to build, configure and use GenroPy Runner: a Tauri 2 desktop app that loads one GenroPy instance in a window without address bar or tabs, and lets the GenroPy page sign with a smart card through PKCS#11.
The project lives in ~/Sviluppo/tauri. The signing logic is a Rust port of firmatore_mac/tessere.py from icond, branch firma-digitale-protocolli.
purpose.diagram: sequenceDiagram participant Server as GenroPy server participant Page as GenroPy page participant Runner as Runner (Rust) participant PinWindow as PIN window participant Card as Card (PKCS#11) Page->>Server: RPC: digest of the document Server-->>Page: SHA-256 digest (32 bytes) Page->>Runner: invoke card_sign(card, digest) alt card closed Runner->>PinWindow: open local window PinWindow->>Runner: pin_submit(pin) Runner->>Card: login(pin) end Runner->>Card: sign(DigestInfo + digest) Card-->>Runner: RSA signature Runner-->>Page: signature (base64) Page->>Server: RPC: signature + certificate

list.item: Rust stable (verified with 1.91) and the Tauri CLI 2: cargo install tauri-cli --version "^2" --locked.
macOS: Xcode or its command line tools. Windows: WebView2, preinstalled on Windows 10 and 11.
For signing: the bit4id PKCS#11 library on the machine. On Windows it comes with Firma4NG of InfoCamere, at 32 bit only.
Node is not needed: the local pages are plain HTML and JavaScript, with no bundler.

step.title: Build and run in development
step.p: cargo tauri dev works as well; arguments for the app go after -- --.

step.title: Set the instance URL
step.p: At startup the URL is taken from the first source that has one:

list.item: --url <address> on the command line, for that launch only.
url in config.json, in the app config directory: ~/Library/Application Support/it.softwell.genropy.runner/ on macOS, %APPDATA%\it.softwell.genropy.runner\ on Windows.
Neither: the setup window asks for the URL and saves it in config.json.

step.p: The menu Instance → Change URL… (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+U) reopens the setup window. Instance → Reload (Cmd/Ctrl+R) reloads the page. Only http and https URLs are accepted.
pkcs11_library and session_minutes are optional. Without pkcs11_library the runner looks for the bit4id library in its default locations.

step.title: Sign from the GenroPy page
step.p: The page in the main window calls three commands through window.__TAURI__.core.invoke. Outside the runner window.__TAURI__ does not exist: the page can test it to show or hide the signing controls.

example.title: Calls from the page

list.item: A card is identified by the sha256 of its signing certificate (keyUsage nonRepudiation), never by the reader.
certificate is the DER certificate in base64: the server needs it to build the PAdES or CAdES signature.
If the card is closed, card_sign opens a local PIN window and waits. The PIN is typed there and never reaches the page.
The PIN window does not try the PIN when the card signals its last attempt or a locked PIN, nor when the PIN length is outside the card limits.
After a right PIN the card stays open for session_minutes: later signatures need no PIN.
Closing the PIN window or pressing Cancel makes card_sign fail with PIN cancelled.

step.p: The server side prepares the digest and assembles the signed file: PDF and pyHanko stay on the server. In icond the RPCs for this flow from the page do not exist yet.

step.title: Build the app for distribution
step.p: The .app starts with a double click. Mac Intel needs a universal build:
step.code: rustup target add x86_64-apple-darwin cargo tauri build --target universal-apple-darwin
step.p: Windows needs a 32-bit build, because the bit4id DLL of Firma4NG is 32-bit only and a 64-bit process cannot load it. It must be built on Windows:
step.code: rustup target add i686-pc-windows-msvc cargo tauri build --target i686-pc-windows-msvc

step.title: Check the permissions
step.p: Serve a test page on localhost and open it with --url. The page calls the commands and prints the result.
step.code: python3 -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1 # in the folder with test.html ./target/debug/genropy-runner --url http://localhost:8765/test.html

list.item: From the configured origin, card_list and card_sign reach the Rust code. Without the library they answer PKCS#11 library not found.
From the same page, get_url and pin_submit are refused with not allowed on window "main".
After navigating to another origin (127.0.0.1 instead of localhost), card_list and card_sign are refused too.

rule.why: The bit4id DLL of Firma4NG is 32-bit only.

rules.rule: Build the Windows app for i686-pc-windows-msvc.

rule.why: A remote page could read it.

rules.rule: Ask the PIN from the GenroPy page. The PIN window of the runner is the only place where it is typed.

rule.why: Any page loaded in the window would get them.

rules.rule: Grant card_* through a static capability with a wildcard origin. The runner grants them at startup to the origin of the configured URL only.

rule.why: tessere.py, test of 2026-11-02: reader order changes between launches.

rules.rule: Identify a card by its certificate fingerprint, not by the reader.

limits.limit: Signing with a real card is not tested: the build machine has no bit4id library.
The Windows 32-bit build and the universal macOS build are not done yet.
The app is signed ad hoc, with no Team ID: on another Mac Gatekeeper blocks it until it is notarized.
Not ported from icond: reload of the library after the Mac sleeps, detection of readers plugged in after launch.
A granted origin keeps the card commands until the app exits, also after Change URL.
Downloads and popups (window.open) from the GenroPy page are not tested.
While a card is open, the page can ask signatures without a new PIN, as with the icond agent. There is no confirmation per signature.

facts.fact: With --url https://example.com the window opens on that page, without address bar, with the host as title and the Instance menu.
Without --url and without config.json the setup window opens.
The card commands answer the configured origin and are refused to another origin in the same window.
The GenroPy page cannot call get_url nor pin_submit.
The card signs the SHA-256 DigestInfo prefix followed by the 32-byte digest, with mechanism CKM_RSA_PKCS, as tessere.py does.
The default macOS library is /Library/bit4id/pkcs11/libbit4xpki.dylib; on Windows the UKC, Firma4NG and System32 copies of bit4xpki.dll, in that order.
cargo tauri build produces the .app and the .dmg for arm64; the .app starts with open.

decision.question: How does a signing request reach the app?

option.title: Directly from the page
option.p: The page calls card_sign and gets the signature at once. Signing needs the runner open on that page.

option.title: Polling like the icond agent
option.p: The app asks icond every 30 seconds with a token. Signing works with the window closed.

decision.choice: One app for window and signing, no polling.

decision.question: Electron or Tauri?

option.title: Tauri 2
option.p: System webview (WebKit on macOS, WebView2 on Windows); bundle around 11 MB.

decision.choice: Smaller bundle; native code in Rust.
